editorial.letter_headline: A Tuesday with one departure in it

wiki_paras: Robert Pattinson topped Wikipedia's most-read list with 1,363,657 views. Ramayana: Part 1 came second on 551,941 and Archive of Our Own third on 463,687. The lead over second place works out at 2.5 times, a margin that leaves the rest of the table looking like a different contest.

The data offers a partial explanation. His name also appears in YouTube's trending cluster, so at least two feeds were looking at him in the same minute. Suki Waterhouse sits fourth on 378,948 views, close by on the list. What drew readers there in the first place, the snapshot does not say.

First and fourth place are separated by almost a million views, and the middle of the table belongs to a film and a fan fiction archive. It is an ordinary Tuesday list with one very large entry on it. Everything below that entry is, by comparison, rounding.
letter_paras: The snapshot found a day with one dominant story and a good deal of weather around it. Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia appears on the news wire, in the prediction markets and on Wikipedia, which is about as close to agreement as these feeds get. The rest is scattered: an actor, a game trailer, a large earthquake.

In the unglamorous corners, BugMeNot closed and collected 439 points on Hacker News, Bluesky stopped to remember Clark Gable 66 years on, and Google Trends in Germany produced Bavendorf, a name the data declines to explain. A Mastodon user is meanwhile watching people assemble outage conspiracies.

A same-minute snapshot catches what a daily summary smooths over. Today the Nvidia exit and an 11 percent market on his return sit side by side, unreconciled. Tomorrow's page will hold a different set, and the comparison between the two is the point. Trends only show up for someone who kept the early pages.

brief: Nvidia without Jensen Huang is the story the feeds agree on: three of the five wire headlines concern his exit, Polymarket gives 11 percent to his return by December 31, and Wikipedia has taken notice. Robert Pattinson still led the encyclopedia with 1,363,657 views, 2.5 times the runner-up. Elsewhere, a magnitude 6.6 earthquake near Tual, Indonesia, and Counter-Strike 2 at 1,089,270 players.
